headline: SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son said AI will become 1,000 times smarter than humans and that slowing it down is the wrong answer.
score_reason: Pool score kept: strong forecast from a major AI investor, but a forecast and an interview of unstated date.
importance_line: Son runs one of the biggest AI investors, so his stance shapes where large sums go, but the 1,000-times figure is his prediction, not a finding.
summary: 36Kr reports, from an interview on Blackstone's internal podcast, that Masayoshi Son, founder, chairman and chief executive of the Japanese investment group SoftBank, predicts AI will be about 1,000 times smarter than humans, possibly within ten years, and said "I do not advocate actually slowing down" because technology development is the solution to AI safety problems. He said SoftBank has more than 30 robotics companies in its portfolio and has started mass production of robots in a factory where robots build robots.
notes: Interview date not stated; reported 14 Oct 2026. English text appears translated, so quotes may be back-translated. Blackstone is a US investment firm (named in the article only as the podcast host).
